clue.text: Duke slightly off dead-centre hits celebratory events

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
on a target the inner is the ring just outside the bull, so hits there are inners

explanation.surface: A duke's slightly wayward darts or arrows still score at festive gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits' looks like a verb joining the halves, but it belongs to the wordplay: shots landing in the inner ring of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal dinners are banquets held to mark occasions, so they are celebratory events.

clue.text: Yes for a Muscovite corporation's immutable point

parts.note: da is Russian for yes
corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: The Russian word for yes as a fixed point in a company's policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation looks like a business, but it is an old slang word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum point is a fixed reference from which measurements are taken.

clue.text: Difficulty in characteristic group composition

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the one that follows

parts.note: a note is a distinguishing quality
a net is a snare, a fix one is caught in

explanation.surface: Trouble in getting the typical group piece written.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonette is a piece of music for nine players, a composition for a group.

clue.text: Note lout accepting good fortune locally — bat's face may show it

parts.note: N is short for note

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for the lout holds the next piece

parts.note: a lout is an oaf
sele is a dialect word for happiness or luck

explanation.surface: A thug welcomes a stroke of luck, and some creature's face may display it.
explanation.walkthrough: Locally means the word is dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose-leaf is the leaf-shaped flap of skin on the snout of certain bats, used in echolocation.

clue.text: This is an act of cleaning up preposterous trend

indicators.note: preposterous literally means the rear part first, so the word is read end to beginning

parts.note: a tide is a current or trend

explanation.surface: A complaint that some absurd fashion is being passed off as a clean-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Preposterous is used in its root sense, before-behind.
explanation.definitionFit: An edit tidies up a text, removing errors, so it is a cleaning-up job.

clue.text: Spiced rum is honest confederate's quirk?

indicators.note: spiced means changed by mixing in other things, so the following letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of rum is honest rearranged

explanation.surface: Spiced rum is described as honest, a peculiar trait of an ally.
explanation.walkthrough: Confederate looks like a mere accomplice; the question mark hints at the Confederate states of the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: A southernism is a word or habit typical of the American South, as a Confederate would show.

clue.text: Chip shot's ending close to a bed of roses?

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of the preceding word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of shot

parts.words: close to a bed of roses
parts.note: a bed of roses is a life of comfort, and ease comes close to that

explanation.surface: A golfer's chip shot finishes up near a rose bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chip shot' reads as golf, but Chip is the definition, in its sense of gently mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip at someone is to make fun of them lightly, which is what it means to tease.

clue.text: Translator poorly represents bit of birdsong

parts.note: TR is an abbreviation for translator
poorly means unwell

explanation.surface: A bad translator mangles a passage of birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: A trill is a rapid warbling run of notes in a bird's song.

clue.text: Previously sufferin' similar

parts.note: surface reading: someone was in pain before
setter's reading: the old spelling ake for ache, with the dropped g, is a word for alike

explanation.surface: Someone who once suffered is now like others.
explanation.walkthrough: Ake is an obsolete spelling of ache, so an archaic achin' or sufferin' reads as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being akin means related or of the same kind, so similar.

clue.text: Squeal and squeal finding free spirit

parts.note: to sing is to inform to the police
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Shrieking and shrieking until one finds liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Both squeals mean informing, not screaming.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an unattached person, someone single and so free.

clue.text: Last of these rather tangle in places causing a mess

indicators.note: last of keeps only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: final letter of these
rather! is an emphatic yes
ore is a dialect word for seaweed, which tangle also means

explanation.surface: The last of these would sooner get knotted up in spots, making a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tangle is a kind of seaweed, not a knot; in places marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly sight, something that looks a mess.

clue.text: Chap who's becoming a success, smashing doors with it

indicators.note: something smashed is broken to pieces, so the letters of the next word are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
to make a go of something is to make a success of it
the letters of doors rearranged
't is the clipped form of it, as in 'tis

explanation.surface: A man on the up kicks in doors as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T for it is an old contraction, as in 'twas and 'tis.
explanation.definitionFit: A good sort is an informal phrase for a decent, likeable person, a good chap.

clue.text: It's nice shifting blame virtually in the manner of eg lab worker

definitions.text: in the manner of eg lab worker

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters of the opening words change places
virtually means almost entirely, so the word before it loses its last letter

parts.note: the letters of it's nice rearranged
to give someone stick is to criticise them

explanation.surface: A pleasant way of passing the buck, typical of a lab worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientistic means in the style of a scientist, often implying excessive faith in scientific method.

clue.text: Containers left unsafely herein

indicators.note: herein says the letters sit inside the words just given, running across the word break

parts.note: spans the end of left and the start of unsafely

explanation.surface: Some containers have been left lying around in an unsafe way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for wine or beer, so tuns are storage vessels.

clue.text: Prompt wrapping is "on trend" for Raymond Blanc's cooking

indicators.note: wrapping means the first word goes round the words that follow it

parts.note: a cue prompts an actor
taken as written
something fashionable is in

explanation.surface: A trendy wrap is suggested as the menu for a celebrity French chef.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Blanc is a French chef who runs a famous restaurant in England, and cuisine is the French word for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of cooking, and the French word fits a French chef's food.

clue.text: New design with arm in the way of a spoon

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters are formed into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh design for cutlery, with an arm on a spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoon is an old word for a fool or a soppy lover, not cutlery; a gander, the male goose, is also a simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganderism is the silly behaviour of a gander, a foolish man, so the way of a spoon or simpleton.

clue.text: Sparrows fool fish

parts.note: tit is a slang word for a fool
ling are long-bodied sea fish; fish works as a plural

explanation.surface: Little birds make fools of the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits birds against fish; fool is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Titling is a dialect name for the hedge sparrow (and for the meadow pipit).

clue.text: Look after dull swabby

indicators.note: after says the first-named word is placed behind the one that follows it

parts.note: matt or mat means without shine
lo is an old word for look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on a boring deckhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' wants to mean take care of, but after is only telling you the order: look's piece follows dull's.
explanation.definitionFit: Swabby is US slang for a sailor who swabs decks, and matlo is British slang for a seaman.

clue.text: Pastry leaf where nothing goes right

indicators.note: goes right says that one piece leaves its place and travels to the right-hand end

parts.note: foil is metal beaten into a thin leaf
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a sheet of pastry with nothing turning right.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the O out of the word for a leaf and put it on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Filo is a paper-thin Greek pastry, rolled out into sheets.

clue.text: We spin yarns about leaving base first in disorderly fashion

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the following words

parts.note: A is an abbreviation of about
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Storytellers wander about, leaving base camp first in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibsters are people who tell fibs, and to spin yarns is to tell tall stories.

clue.text: Bloody concerned with niece and rent being awry

indicators.note: awry means out of position, so the letters before it are put into a different order

parts.note: to be in something is to be involved with it
the letters of niece and rent rearranged

explanation.surface: A family row over a niece and unpaid rent turns ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: Internecine conflict is destructive and murderous to both sides, hence bloody.

clue.text: ____, its cure gets complicated

indicators.note: something that gets complicated is tangled, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of its cure rearranged

explanation.surface: Treating some unnamed illness is proving difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank stands for the answer, which completes the sentence about a hard-to-treat condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Icterus is the medical name for jaundice, a disease that needs a cure.

clue.text: Greek character, demagogue, is a fundamental constituent

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Cleon was a notorious Athenian demagogue

explanation.surface: A Greek rabble-rouser described as a basic part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon is a proton or neutron, a basic particle of the atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Practically passing credit withdraw from the art world

indicators.note: practically means nearly all, so the word after it loses its last letter

parts.note: passing is a euphemism for dying
a tribute gives someone credit for what they did

explanation.surface: An artist's credit is being almost carelessly taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: To deattribute a painting is to stop crediting it to a named artist, an art-historian's term.

clue.text: Wanting tips for each offence harass grass

indicators.note: wanting tips for each says every word in the phrase loses an end letter where the two meet

parts.note: to tee off is slang for to anger, give offence, needle someone

explanation.surface: Someone is rid of the cash for each offence of harassing a grass, an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose the last letter of the first word and the first of the second, where they touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Teff is an Ethiopian cereal grass whose seed is ground for flour.

clue.text: Poet's grievous euphemism for damn concerning

parts.note: dee is a mild substitute for damn
re means about

explanation.surface: A poet's sad talk about a softened curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Poet's marks a word from Spenser and older verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Deere is a Spenserian spelling of dere, meaning dire or grievous.

clue.text: Supposed bringer of good luck to team scoring first in tie

indicators.note: scoring means crossing out, so the opening letter is struck through

parts.words: Supposed bringer of good luck to team
parts.note: a team mascot is meant to bring luck

explanation.surface: A team's lucky charm leads to scoring first in a cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring first' sounds like sport, but here it means striking out the first letter. Tie is a noun, the neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad cravat, a kind of neck tie.

clue.text: Street supporting choice cattle-fair

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so the first-named word goes below the next

parts.note: try is an old adjective meaning choice or excellent
ST is short for street

explanation.surface: A street holding up the best cattle at a market.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, supporting puts the street underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Tryst is a Scots word for a market or fair, especially for cattle.

clue.text: Question Cupid about backing inflexible one

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so Cupid's name encloses what follows

parts.note: Eros is the Greek counterpart of Cupid

indicators.note: backing means running backwards, so the word next to it is read from its end

parts.note: set in one's ways
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Cupid is quizzed about supporting someone stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotesis is the rhetorical figure of asking a question that expects or implies an answer.

clue.text: It's at the heart of reports air-traffic control put up

definitions.text: It's at the heart of reports air-traffic control put up

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of reports

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means raised, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A unit central to the reports issued by air-traffic control.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a unit used in airport weather reports.
explanation.definitionFit: An okta or octa is an eighth of the sky, the unit for cloud cover in aviation weather reports.

clue.text: No longer cut a cynical facial expression endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a sneer is a scornful look

explanation.surface: A cynical look is cut off, and no longer seen.
explanation.walkthrough: No longer marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Snee is an obsolete form of snick or sny, meaning to cut.

clue.text: Boobs — complaint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: blunders, plural of a slang word for a howler
second meaning: a bone disease of children

explanation.walkthrough: A ricket is a slang term for a mistake, so the plural matches boobs; the disease is a separate word used only in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a childhood disorder of soft bones, and a complaint is an illness.

clue.text: Partial to a pint out of barrels? Spooky

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so the abbreviation that follows is removed

parts.note: fond of drinking beer
B is an abbreviation for barrels

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a pint being kept from the barrels finds it eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Eery is a variant spelling of eerie, uncanny and frightening.

clue.text: Having three bits to cut back or use differently

indicators.note: differently means done another way, so the words before it are put in a new order

parts.note: to trim is to cut back
the letters of or use rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for something in three parts: prune it or find another purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimerous is a botanical term for flowers whose parts come in threes.

clue.text: Is confusingly complex system what obscures the view?

parts.note: is is shortened to 's, as in it's
a maze is a bewildering network

explanation.surface: A question asking whether some baffling set-up is what blocks one's vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusingly' looks like it calls for a shuffle, but it simply describes the network.
explanation.definitionFit: Smaze is a blend of smoke and haze, a pollution that reduces visibility.

clue.text: Nibble you don't see much now — supply ten such

definitions.text: Nibble you don't see much now

indicators.note: supply is read as the adverb, in a supple way, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: the letters of ten such rearranged

explanation.surface: A snack that has gone out of fashion, and someone is asked to provide ten of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' wants to be a verb; read it as supple-ly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesnut is an archaic spelling of chestnut, a nut eaten as a snack.
